status.en: 5 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 55% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Oromo.
status.nb: 5 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 55 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Oromo.

summary.en: Ethiopian and Eritrean forces are massing troops along their shared border, while clashes between Ethiopian militia and Somali Federalist Party supporters in Moyale have displaced thousands and prompted the EU to provide about Sh80 million in emergency aid. A drone strike near Badme wounded four civilians, and a Bioengineer.org study reports high rates of suicidal behavior among conflict-affected Ethiopian high schoolers. The conflict has already caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske og eritreiske styrker samler tropper langs deres felles grense, mens sammenstøt mellom etiopisk milits og støttespillere til Somali Federalist Party i Moyale har fordrevet tusenvis og fått EU til å gi omtrent 80 millioner shilling i nødhjelp. Et droneangrep nær Badme såret fire sivile, og en studie fra Bioengineer.org rapporterer høye forekomster av selvmordstendenser blant konflikt-påvirkede etiopiske videregåendeelever. Konflikten har allerede forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
